card.title: Protected Areas, Biodiversity Hotspots and Endangered Species

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Wildlife sustains ecology and economy alike — pollinating crops, dispersing seeds, drawing tourists, storing genetic resources and carrying ethical worth. Its loss accelerates through habitat destruction, overexploitation, pollution, invasive species, disease and climate change, on top of the natural background rate; small populations then fall into the extinction vortex of inbreeding and drift.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Extinct (EX) vs Extinct in the Wild (EW):** EX means no individuals survive anywhere; EW means survivors exist only in captivity/cultivation.  ·  **Threatened vs endangered:** "threatened" is the umbrella for CR, EN and VU; "endangered" is one specific category within it.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short answer (2m): What does Data Deficient (DD) mean?** — The IUCN category for species with too little information to assess their extinction risk; they may prove threatened once studied — research priority, not safety.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most likely items: IUCN categories with Nepal examples; three extinction causes with mechanisms; three conservation strategies with examples; extinction vortex.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **The extinction vortex:** small populations inbreed, lose fitness and shrink further — a genetic feedback loop that outlives the original threat.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Wildlife value: ecological (pollination, dispersal, pest control), economic (tourism), scientific (bioindicators), genetic (wild crop relatives), aesthetic-ethical, medicinal.  ·  Extinction causes: habitat destruction, overexploitation, pollution, invasives, disease, climate change (plus natural background causes).  ·  Conservation: in-situ parks, ex-situ zoos/seed banks/translocation, law (CITES, CBD, Ramsar), community conservation, restoration, education.  ·  IUCN: EX, EW, CR, EN, VU, NT, LC, DD; threatened = CR+EN+VU. Nepal: gharial CR, tiger/red panda/arna EN, rhino/snow leopard VU.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The current extinction rate is estimated at hundreds of times the natural background rate — the sixth mass extinction, human-driven.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Why Wildlife Matters and Why It Vanishes Wildlife's value spans ecology (pollination, seed dispersal, nutrient cycling), economy (tourism, medicine, genetics), science (research, indicator species) and ethics (every species' right to exist). Extinction is natural — but the current rate, driven by humans, is hundreds of times the background rate.…  ·  ## 2. Importance of Wildlife | Domain | Contributions | |---|---| | **Ecological** | Pollination (bees, bats), seed dispersal (birds, monkeys), nutrient cycling, pest control (insectivorous birds), population regulation | | **Economic** | Tourism revenue (tiger- and rhino-watching in Nepal), timber and non-timber forest products, fisheries | | **Scientific** | Model organisms…  ·  ## 3. Causes of Extinction | Cause | Mechanism | Example | |---|---|---| | **Habitat destruction and fragmentation** | Forests cleared, rivers dammed, land converted | Terai forest loss; road fragmentation | | **Overexploitation** | Hunting, poaching, overfishing beyond recovery | Rhino poaching for horn; tiger poaching for bone | | **Pollution** | Toxins accumulate or degrade…
